hot.title: H-JEPA: End-to-End Learning of Hierarchical World Models for Visual Planning
hot.summary: H-JEPA plans visual tasks by learning three predictive levels, with each higher level predicting farther ahead in its own latent space and passing subgoals to finer planners. In a 50-task simulated AntMaze evaluation, three-level H-JEPA reaches 73.3% success, versus 18.0% for flat LeWM. A separate compute sweep shows a higher-success, lower-planner-compute frontier, not a wall-clock speedup; evidence is from simulation and offline DROID evaluation.

hot.title: QF3: Fast Flow RL with Filtered Q-Gradients
hot.summary: QF3 addresses robot learning by improving flow policies from replayed experience. It anchors policy updates to replay actions through flow matching, then applies a critic gradient to a one-step action prediction, clipping velocity corrections that stray too far from the replay target. In tested settings, clipping prevents collapse; on G1 dance tracking, training reaches full episodes about 10 times faster than FPO++.

hot.title: Kernel Autoresearch for Open-Ended Model Discovery
hot.summary: KERNAUT uses language-model coding agents to discover reusable Gaussian-process kernels as programs, while a trusted interpreter assembles proposals through positive-semidefinite-preserving constructions. Across several benchmarks, selected kernels improved on fixed or learned references in some settings—including an 8.3% mean test-CRPS reduction in black-box optimization campaigns and a strong enzyme-kinetics result—though benefits varied by task and were not universal.

hot.title: Long-WAM: Scaling the Context of World-Action Models
hot.summary: Long-WAM trains a robot controller to predict future video from visual history, then uses those predictions to generate actions. On RoboCasa GR-1, robot-domain autoregressive initialization raises success from 66.3% with 2.4 seconds of history to 78.7% with 19.2 seconds, while bidirectional initialization stays near 62%. This simulated comparison supports, but does not prove, the explanation that autoregressive pretraining helps use history.

hot.title: OpenWAM: An Open Framework for Composable World-Action Models
hot.summary: OpenWAM tests links between video predictions and robot actions, including reuse of action models. It compares generation routes in a shared framework and trains separate dynamics models on demonstrations and counterfactual transitions. After target-task video adaptation, a frozen local-context inverse dynamics model achieves 84.0% mean closed-loop success across four held-out LIBERO-90 simulation targets, versus 47.0% for full-context conditioning.

hot.title: EmbodiedRSI: Active Continual Robot Learning Through Hypothesis-Guided Co-Evolution
hot.summary: EmbodiedRSI adapts a robot harness around a frozen vision-language-action model by maintaining competing code and skill hypotheses, selecting simulator experiments for expected information gain relative to cost, and retaining useful evidence. On RoboCasa365’s Composite-Unseen suite, it reports 71.3% success, versus 40.1% for Harness VLA. This supports harness-level adaptation on tested tasks, not model learning or universal gains.

hot.title: RSIGym: A Flexible Environment for Recursive Self-Improvement
hot.summary: RSIGym provides reusable services for training, inference, rollouts, evaluation, and sandbox computation, while permissions let agents change data, training settings, harnesses, or combinations. In one budgeted run, six agents improved 29 of 30 settings across five benchmarks. Opus 5 achieved an RSI-Index of 0.4809 and raised SWE-bench Verified from 17.67% to 50.33%. The results do not establish progress across later cycles.

hot.title: VeriFine: Scaling Verification for Self-Improvement in Embodied Reasoning
hot.summary: VeriFine adapts a policy, its curriculum, and its judge as failures change. Its reference-free rubric judge evaluates reasoning against context, while policy and judge loops select examples and have humans refine unreliable judgments. Across three driving rounds, reasoning scores rise from 60.56 to 71.61, an 18.2% relative gain; evidence covers driving and robot navigation, not every task.

hot.title: Optimal and Efficient Online Inverse Optimization
hot.summary: The paper presents online inverse linear optimization with revocable directional updates, learning from expert choices without observing the hidden objective or utility values. The deterministic, proper RVM learner removes a stretch after its query leaves a slab and achieves regret at most 51√d/4 for every horizon; a matching-order lower bound applies when T≥d.

hot.title: Sherpa: Teaching LLMs to Teach Adaptively
hot.summary: Sherpa trains a math tutor through multi-turn interactions with simulated students whose instructional preferences affect which guidance they accept, rewarding the tutor by the student’s later problem-solving performance. On the filtered math evaluation, its Qwen3-8B teacher reached 69.0% average post-tutoring accuracy across seven student archetypes, versus 48.6% for the untrained teacher; this does not establish learning gains in real students.

hot.title: Recursive Game Creator: An Agentic Product-Level Experience-Oriented Game Harness
hot.summary: Recursive Game Creator refines games through repeated play-and-review cycles. A Designer plans changes, a Builder creates candidates, executable policies play through structured game interfaces, and a Reviewer uses gameplay records, visual evidence, and preferences to guide revisions. On GameCraft-Bench, GPT-6 Astra (high) Overall scores rise from 72.70 to 77.89; these benchmark scores do not measure human enjoyment.

hot.title: RoboJEPA: Scaling Robotic Latent World Models
hot.summary: RoboJEPA predicts future visual features under robot actions and uses imagined outcomes to plan toward a goal image. Its predictor scales from 22 million to 8 billion parameters while keeping the V-JEPA 2.1 encoder fixed. A second-order compute law extrapolates held-out prediction error better than a standard power law, but does not establish a universal link to robot success.

hot.title: SGF+: Decoupling Gradient Flows for Autoregressive Video Generation
hot.summary: SGF+ separates context writing from denoising in autoregressive video generation, while allowing predictions to read the written history. It uses distinct parameters for the two roles and trains them through a shared generation objective. In 240-second framewise tests, it scores higher than SGF on Subject and Background Consistency, but lower on Dynamic Degree; 24-hour generation is qualitative, not quantitatively benchmarked.

hot.title: Preserving Unstable Modes Through Inverse Dynamics in JEPA World Models
hot.summary: The authors introduce EP-IDM, which trains a world model to predict future latent states and reconstruct action sequences from endpoint latents. For linear systems, exact reconstruction under sufficient action excitation preserves information on reachable directions. In simulated CartPole, latent LQR success rises from 0% with SIGReg to 100% with EP-IDM; however, SIGReg models also succeed under nonlinear replanning.

hot.title: Base Models Can Reason By Taking a Cue From Training Data
hot.summary: The authors test whether short fixed openings can elicit reasoning from language models without changing their weights. On MATH-500, Olmo-3-7B pass@1 rises from 42% without a cue to 78% with “Okay,” versus 75% after reinforcement learning. In a controlled data-edit experiment, renaming “okay” to “chicken” makes “Chicken” effective, supporting cue effects in these tested settings, not all models.

hot.title: GRACE: Generation-aware latent compression for efficient video generation
hot.summary: GRACE compresses video latents for pretrained diffusion transformers. It combines a coarse base latent from the pretrained encoder with a learned residual, aligns compressed representations to frozen DiT features, and denoises the base ahead of the residual. At 480×832×81, it uses 4.3k rather than 32.8k tokens, with I2V VBench Total scores of 87.90 and 87.92, respectively.

hot.title: EigenDEXplore: Structured Exploration for Dexterous Manipulation with Human Priors
hot.summary: EigenDEXplore guides robot exploration with coordinated patterns learned from retargeted human hand motion, while retaining joint-by-joint control. It combines independent joint noise with noise along principal-component directions. After 9 billion frames in five-seed SimToolReal tests, it reaches 10.6 consecutive object-pose goals versus 7.9 for Joint-Space. Across four real-robot tasks, mean waypoint progress is 82% versus 33%, within the tested setup.

hot.title: Building Rome from a Single Image
hot.summary: The method reconstructs a scene mesh from one photograph by varying generation-region size with depth and conditioning geometry generation on estimated surface locations and visibility cues. On seven Tanks and Temples scenes, it reports normalized Chamfer distance 1.99 versus VolFill’s 2.63, and F1 0.506 versus Lyra 2.0’s 0.388; hidden geometry is plausible completion, not observed fact.

hot.title: IdeaAnchor: Teaching LLMs to Turn Literature into Research Ideas
hot.summary: IdeaAnchor trains language models to propose research directions by learning structured links between prior papers and criteria derived from published contributions. Its training anchors identify paper roles, relationships, and requirements for coherent proposals, but are withheld at deployment. On the ICLR 2026 benchmark, RL-trained Qwen3.5-9B achieved 54.2% criteria satisfaction, versus 31.1% for its base; this measures written proposals, not research success.

hot.title: RobotWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Robot Use Across Diverse Tasks and Embodiments
hot.summary: RobotWorld evaluates whether tool-using AI agents can complete robot tasks across five domains. It benchmarks 84 tasks from 20 projects, using task-specific interfaces, interaction budgets, and executable success checks. The authors analyze execution traces to examine how perception, computation, and feedback-driven action compose. GPT-6 Astra completes 16/84 tasks, the highest result. The benchmark is simulation-only, with one episode per model-task pair.

likes.title: Towards Looped Models Done Right Part II: Rethinking at Fixed Points
likes.summary: The paper trains a looped language model to settle toward fixed points across repeated applications of a shared block. Terminal key-value (KV) sharing retains only final cache banks; separate methods reuse endpoints for prefill and reinforcement learning. At 1.6B parameters, the learned-depth-prior model scores 60.00% on the downstream average with four rather than twelve KV banks, in the reported setup.

likes.title: Finetuning with Sampling: SFT Learns Better Than You Think
likes.summary: Projection sampling transforms expert demonstrations into responses more like those of a pretrained model before standard supervised fine-tuning, using the model to propose continuations and an MCMC procedure to select them. On Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, it raises SciKnowEval Chemistry L-3 single-shot accuracy to 66.0%, while the five-task prior-capability average is 58.6%, below the base model’s 59.7%.

likes.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
likes.summary: ScholarCatalyst benchmarks whether systems can retrieve prior papers that project authors judged helpful or potentially helpful to early-stage research. It uses 894 retrospectively annotated queries from 207 computer-science projects, with author-labeled positives and hard negatives. Across its reported settings, agentic search reaches overall Recall@20 of 0.42 versus 0.48 for embedding retrieval, measuring retrospective judgments rather than successful inspiration.

likes.title: VISTA: A Visual Harness for Reasoning in an Interactive World
likes.summary: VISTA gives a multimodal model access to archived game frames, allowing it to retrieve earlier images, compare moments, and enlarge details while reasoning in language and choosing actions. Across 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games, Claude Opus 5.0 completes all games with a mean Relative Human Action Efficiency score of 100.00, using 7,302 actions versus 17,135 for first-time humans. This public-set result does not establish performance on unseen games.

likes.title: Decoding Looped Transformers Better for (Almost) Free
likes.summary: LoopCD guides looped Transformers by extrapolating from an earlier prediction toward the final prediction for the same prefix, without adding recurrent iterations. It offers logits and hidden-state variants, with hidden-state guidance avoiding an extra output pass. On AIME 2024, adaptive LoopCD-Logits raises Ouro-2.6B-Thinking pass@1 from 61.88% to 73.33%; results are not uniformly positive across tasks and metrics.

likes.title: Introducing Beam: Reflection’s 501B open-weight model
likes.summary: Reflection introduces Beam, its first open-weight model: a sparse Mixture-of-Experts with 501 billion total and 23 billion active parameters, aimed at coding, reasoning, and agentic workloads. It was pretrained on 23.8 trillion curated tokens and then trained with a high-compute reinforcement learning run of over 100 million rollouts on 10.5K NVIDIA GB300 GPUs. Beam is competitive with larger open models while using far less inference compute, and its weights are slated for release under Apache 2.0 later in the month.

likes.title: LiFT: Loop Flow Transformers
likes.summary: LiFT uses a shared transformer core within each diffusion step, training passes to refine velocity estimates along a correction path. On class-conditional ImageNet-1k at 256×256, LiFT-L/2 R10 run with eight loops and 50 steps reaches FID 10.95 at 28.24 TFLOPs per image, versus dense DiT-XL/2 with 250 steps at FID 14.30. This unguided, cross-scale comparison does not establish latency savings or generalization.

likes.title: Truly Subquadratic 3SUM and Truly Subcubic APSP via Triangles in Sparse Lopsided Graphs
likes.summary: The authors introduce a deterministic algorithm that computes selected entries of a thin matrix product without computing the full product or each entry separately. It recursively multiplies rectangular matrices and prunes work for unrequested outputs. It gives 3SUM in O(n^1.9992) and directed APSP in O(n^2.9995) for polynomially bounded integers in the word-RAM model, asymptotic bounds rather than measured speedups.

On MATH-500, Olmo-3-7B pass@1 rises from 42% without a cue to 78% with “Okay,” versus 75% after reinforcement learning. In a controlled data-edit experiment, renaming “okay” to “chicken” makes “Chicken” effective, supporting cue effects in these tested settings, not all models.

likes.title: Kolibri: A Sovereign European Model on the Pareto Frontier
likes.summary: Kolibri is an open-weight bilingual model designed for local deployment on controlled infrastructure. It activates 3.46B of 78.1B parameters per token and uses sliding-window attention in 40 of 50 blocks, with full attention in every fifth block. Against Kolibri Origin, its post-trained scores are higher in English and German, with 2.7× reported decode throughput under the paper’s measurement setup.

likes.title: Sphere Encoder 2
likes.summary: Sphere Encoder 2 trains a decoder to reconstruct near encoded points and generate from random points near the sphere’s equator, replacing limited noise and pixel reconstruction loss with rotation-based training and feature-space score matching. On ImageNet at 256×256, Sphere2-L† reports FDr6 4.92 at 4×2 NFE, versus PixNerd-XL’s 5.01 at 100×2 NFE; this compares sampling compute, not wall-clock time.

likes.title: UndoBench: Separating Task Competence from Recovery Capability in Tool-Using AI Agents
likes.summary: The authors introduce UndoBench to evaluate whether AI agents recover safely when external operations fail. It pairs identical-seed control and faulted runs, measuring recovery only when the control succeeds, and records external effects. Across 12 held-out workflows, control success was 83.54%, but conditional recovery was 46.72%; results cover sandboxed trials with one lost acknowledgment fault.

likes.title: Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real: Guided Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
likes.summary: RPG lets robot skills improve through practice without changing model weights. It revises reusable executable skills and system prompts using failure diagnosis, then validates candidate and merged changes across tasks. In simulation, held-out success across 22 manipulation tasks rose from 63/220 (28.6%) after round 1 to 209/220 (95.0%) after round 15; this is not matched-compute evidence.

likes.title: OneStreamer: Unifying Perception, Memory, and Proactive Response in Streaming Video Interaction
likes.summary: OneStreamer addresses streaming video questions by retaining generated, time-grounded captions alongside a recent visual window and producing responses when its control state calls for them. In a controlled comparison using the same checkpoint and Recent-16 window, caption memory raises OVOBench-Backward ASI from 63.5 to 71.6, while real-time scores also rise. The results support these benefits in tested settings, not universally.

likes.title: World Motion Models: Flexible Sequence Modeling of SE(3) Trajectories
likes.summary: World Motion Models (WMMs) represent moving entities as time sequences of rigid poses, with features identifying entity types. By assigning each pose its own noise level, a model can generate unknown poses conditioned on known poses, supporting varied motion tasks. On Language Table, WMM’s macro-average success is 87.2%, versus 80.0% for LCB; results use separate checkpoints per benchmark.

likes.title: Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models
likes.summary: Sigma extends likelihood-trained continuous diffusion language modeling to 3B and 8B parameter models, testing math and code. It represents tokens in a learned 16-dimensional space and iteratively denoises blocks of 32 tokens, with blocks generated sequentially. Across six math and coding tasks, Sigma-3B averages 64.34% pass@1, close to the matched masked-diffusion baseline’s 64.74%; this does not establish faster end-to-end generation.

likes.title: Language Models that Play Chess and Explain Their Moves
likes.summary: QUEEN connects a chess encoder and language model to recommend and explain moves. It learns to use expert representations and fine-tunes on explanations of candidate continuations checked against Stockfish. Its reported estimated rating is 2697 Elo, and its predicted lines avoid Stockfish-defined mistakes in 68.8% of tactical positions, while conceptual coherence scores below structural coherence.

likes.title: UniWAM: Unified World-Action Model
likes.summary: UniWAM trains one robot system to understand scenes, predict future images, and generate actions. It combines visual question-answer data, human video, and robot demonstrations with shared attention and language descriptions of motion. On the 50-task RoboTwin 2.0 evaluation, it reaches 68.32% success in clean-to-randomized testing, the highest among methods listed in the paper’s table.

likes.title: Priced Guidance: Can Language Models Generate Future Research Ideas?
likes.summary: Priced Guidance measures information needed for a model to recover an existing research idea. A generator assigns probabilities to answers; a target-informed guide selects among them, and less likely answers cost more bits. Expected cost bounds unguided acceptance from below. The ensemble’s median Essence cost was 55.8 bits, versus 69.9 for Fable 5.1 alone, measuring guided recovery rather than independent research generation.
